newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO's Arafat hosts Israel's Peres in West Bank.
newsitem.headline: PLO's Arafat hosts Israel's Peres in West Bank.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat met Israeli opposition leader Shimon Peres on Sunday in self-ruled Nablus to discuss now-threatened peace deals which they crafted.
Asked if he was bringing a message to Arafat, Peres told reporters with a smile: "I am the message."
The Palestinian President said he hoped Peres would help push forward stalled peace moves. "I expect from him support for the peace process," Arafat told reporters.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who ousted Nobel Peace prize laureate Peres in May on a platform to slow peace moves with the Palestinians, had agreed to the talks between the two men, who last met on August 22.
Peres, asked by reporters whether the right-wing Netanyahu had jeopardised Israeli-Palestinian peace deals, said: "I don't think the peace process is in danger but it is facing certain difficulties."
"Despite all the difficulties, you should not lose hope," the 73-year-old former prime minister said to Arafat.
They met as Israel's Arab peace partners were slamming the door in Netanyahu's face while reaching out to other Israeli political players.

Israeli relations with Egypt, Jordan and the Palestinians have deteriorated as Netanyahu has stalled implementation of an already long-delayed Israeli redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron agreed more than a year ago.
Peres was summoned to Nablus in the West Bank by Arafat on Sunday and to Egypt by President Hosni Mubarak next week, a spokeswoman for Peres said.
The Hebron redeployment should have been carried out in March but was delayed by Peres after Islamic militant suicide bombers killed 59 people in Israel in February and March.
It was frozen by Netanyahu, who says changes are needed to the deal to ensure the security of 400 Jewish settlers living in enclaves amidst 100,000 Arabs in Hebron.
Palestinians refuse to amend the Hebron accord.

Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said there was "not one inch of progress" in U.S.-brokered Israeli-Palestinian talks due to resume on Monday in Taba, Egypt. He urged Washington to push Israel to keep the deal reached by its previous government.

Peres, meeting Arafat in the last West Bank city still under an Israeli blockade imposed after fierce clashes killed 60 Palestinians and 15 Israelis in September, urged patience while talks continued.
"In the peace process there are ups and downs. When you are up you don't lose your head. When you are down, you shouldn't lose your heart," Peres said.
